- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.0 → 0.4+), model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 30-day MA), model overfits trend; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7 days.
